name: armin
description: Turn articles, notes, documents, and Anki decks into Armin spaced-repetition cards, with prerequisites and a guided, image-preserving Anki import.

interface.longDescription:
Armin is a spaced-repetition flashcard app whose cards form a prerequisite graph: a card stays locked until the cards it depends on are learned, and FSRS schedules every review.

Share an article, lecture notes, a document, or code, and ask for study cards. The model reads the material, writes focused question-and-answer, cloze, reversed, and typed-answer cards, links foundations to the ideas built on them, and saves the deck to your Armin library with a link to start studying.

You approve each connection in Armin. By default a connection can only see and change the decks it creates; you can choose to share existing decks and allow edits. Armin never fetches web pages or runs a model itself. Ordinary card authoring is text-only. A separate guided Anki import can run Armin's versioned converter in your assistant's sandbox, preserve supported images through a narrowly scoped upload, and stage new decks until you approve the final preview. Anki imports always start fresh. The plugin cannot permanently delete cards or decks, change review history, or manage your account. Archiving a card is reversible.

Requires an Armin account at armincards.app.
defaultPrompt: Make study cards in Armin from this article.
Turn my lecture notes into an Armin deck with prerequisites.

positive.description: Create a new deck from pasted material
positive.prompt: Make an Armin deck called HTTP basics from this text: HTTP is a request-response protocol. A client sends a request with a method such as GET or POST, and the server replies with a status code such as 200 or 404.
positive.expected_behavior: Saves several focused cards in a new deck named HTTP basics, links the definition of HTTP as a prerequisite of the method and status-code cards, and returns the deck link.

positive.description: List the decks the connection can access
positive.prompt: Which Armin decks can you see?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists only decks this connection is allowed to access, with their names, and explains that other decks stay private unless shared in Armin.

positive.prompt: Show me the cards in my HTTP basics deck and how they depend on each other.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the deck, lists its cards, and describes the prerequisite links without changing anything.

positive.prompt: In HTTP basics, change the status code card so its answer also mentions 500 Internal Server Error.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the current card and version, updates only that card's answer, and confirms the change.

positive.prompt: Archive the card about POST requests in HTTP basics.
positive.expected_behavior: Archives that one card, explains that archiving hides it from study while keeping its content and review history, and that it can be unarchived.

positive.description: Import an Anki deck with its images
positive.prompt: Import this Anki deck into Armin. Keep the images and show me what needs repair before saving.
positive.expected_behavior: Downloads and verifies Armin's converter kit, runs it locally, stages the converted cards and supported images, lists every unresolved note, asks the user to approve the final preview, and finalizes only after approval. No Anki scheduling history is applied and no prerequisites are invented.

negative.prompt: Permanently delete all my Armin decks.

negative.description: Reviews and scheduling stay in Armin
negative.prompt: Mark all my Armin cards as reviewed and rated Easy today.
Change my Armin password and email address.

negative.description: Silent rewriting during an Anki import is not allowed
negative.prompt: Import this Anki deck and quietly rewrite any cards you think are weak, adding prerequisites where they make sense.

review.commerce_description: Armin does not sell products or process payments through this plugin.

publication.release_notes: Adds a guided, staged Anki import with deterministic conversion, supported image upload, explicit repair or skip decisions, and approval before saving.
